Values.Group: 1. Getting started - Azure tenant and subscription
Values.Label: Tenant ID
Values.Description: The Microsoft Entra tenant (directory) the nodes register into with Azure Arc. Find it in the Azure portal: Microsoft Entra ID -> Overview -> Tenant ID. It's the identity directory, not the subscription. Injected into the Arc registration script so nobody has to type a GUID inside a node. PRIVATE: 'Export for sharing' empties this value.
Values.Hint: A GUID: 8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal characters

Values.Group: 1. Getting started - Azure tenant and subscription
Values.Label: Subscription ID
Values.Description: The Azure subscription the nodes register into, and where the cluster is deployed. Find it in the Azure portal: Subscriptions -> Subscription ID. Once a cluster is deployed, the only way to change its subscription is to redeploy it. PRIVATE: 'Export for sharing' empties this value.
Values.Hint: A GUID: 8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal characters

Values.Group: 1. Getting started - Azure tenant and subscription
Values.Label: Your time zone
Values.Description: The Windows time zone set on the Azure host VM, the domain controller, the admin station and the Azure Local nodes, so every log and event in the lab shows the same local time. Leave it empty and the Lab Builder fills in this PC's time zone when it opens. Use the Windows time zone ID, not an abbreviation like CST. To list the IDs, run:  Get-TimeZone -ListAvailable | Select-Object Id  (the time itself still comes from the DC, which keeps the clocks in step).
Values.Hint: A Windows time zone ID, e.g. Central Standard Time, Eastern Standard Time, Pacific Standard Time, UTC

Values.Group: 2. Azure host VM - super-host for the domain controller, admin station and Azure Local nodes
Values.Label: Host VM size (SKU)
Values.Description: Select an Azure VM SKU or Custom (on-premises). Custom hosts use manually entered SuperHost CPU/RAM, without Azure SKU ceilings or memory matching. Optional Refresh Azure sizes retains the custom option. Azure CPU-support metadata remains advisory; Azure creation is not applicable to a custom host.
Values.Hint: Select an Azure VM SKU or Custom (on-premises). Custom hosts use manually entered SuperHost CPU/RAM, without Azure SKU ceilings or memory matching. Optional Refresh Azure sizes retains the custom option. Azure CPU-support metadata remains advisory; Azure creation is not applicable to a custom host.

Values.Group: 2. Azure host VM - super-host for the domain controller, admin station and Azure Local nodes
Values.Label: Resource group for host VM
Values.Description: The Azure resource group for the super-host VM and everything that belongs to it: its disks, network card, public IP and network security group. Create this first. Keep it SEPARATE from the Azure Local cluster's resource group, so the lab host and the cluster can be managed (and deleted) independently.
Values.Hint: 1-90 letters, numbers, . _ - ( )  and it can't end with a period

Values.Group: 2. Azure host VM - super-host for the domain controller, admin station and Azure Local nodes
Values.Label: Azure CLI - create host VM resource group
Values.Description: One line that creates the HOST VM resource group (for the super-host VM and its disks, NIC, public IP and NSG). Built from the values in groups 1, 2 and 4, so it updates as you change them. DOUBLE-CLICK to copy, then paste into PowerShell after 'az login --tenant <tenant ID>', or into Azure Cloud Shell. Safe to run again - an existing group is left alone.
Values.Hint: Double-click to copy
Values.UsedIn: Your workstation or Azure Cloud Shell, before script 00

Values.Group: 2. Azure host VM - super-host for the domain controller, admin station and Azure Local nodes
Values.Label: Azure VM name
Values.Description: The Azure VM that acts as a super-host for the whole lab: it runs Hyper-V and holds the domain controller (ContosoDC1), the admin station and the Azure Local nodes (2 by default) as nested VMs. Its Windows computer name is the same as the VM name, so keep it to 15 characters or less.
Values.Hint: 1-15 letters, numbers or hyphens, starting with a letter or number

Values.Group: 2. Azure host VM - super-host for the domain controller, admin station and Azure Local nodes
Values.Label: SuperHost available vCPUs (min 20)
Values.Description: Request available vCPUs, default 20. Standard_D48als_v7 maximum is 48. Positive whole-number requests up to the known maximum pass local validation. Missing or unlisted Azure reduced-count metadata warns without blocking copy/rollout; Azure enforces CPU support during creation. Base VM price is unchanged; quota is separate. Lab minimum is 20 available vCPUs. Aggregate guest CPU allocations may exceed this count with a sharing warning; each individual guest must fit this count. For Custom (on-premises), enter the logical processors available to this lab; no Azure SKU ceiling applies.
Values.Hint: Request available vCPUs, default 20. Standard_D48als_v7 maximum is 48. Positive whole-number requests up to the known maximum pass local validation. Missing or unlisted Azure reduced-count metadata warns without blocking copy/rollout; Azure enforces CPU support during creation. Base VM price is unchanged; quota is separate. Lab minimum is 20 available vCPUs. Aggregate guest CPU allocations may exceed this count with a sharing warning; each individual guest must fit this count. For Custom (on-premises), enter the logical processors available to this lab; no Azure SKU ceiling applies.

Values.Group: 2. Azure host VM - super-host for the domain controller, admin station and Azure Local nodes
Values.Label: SuperHost RAM (GB, minimum 96)
Values.Description: Enter the SuperHost RAM available to this lab. Custom (on-premises) uses your manually entered capacity; Azure sizes must match known SKU memory. Actual host capacity is checked before guest creation.
Values.Hint: Enter the SuperHost RAM available to this lab. Custom (on-premises) uses your manually entered capacity; Azure sizes must match known SKU memory. Actual host capacity is checked before guest creation.

Values.Group: 2. Azure host VM - super-host for the domain controller, admin station and Azure Local nodes
Values.Label: Reserve RAM for SuperHost (GB)
Values.Description: RAM kept for the SuperHost OS and Hyper-V, not assigned to guests. Default 16 GB. Guest RAM plus this reserve must fit the host.
Values.Hint: RAM kept for the SuperHost OS and Hyper-V, not assigned to guests. Default 16 GB. Guest RAM plus this reserve must fit the host.

Values.Group: 2. Azure host VM - super-host for the domain controller, admin station and Azure Local nodes
Values.Label: DC vCPUs (minimum 2)
Values.Description: Processors for ContosoDC1. Minimum 2. CPU is shared across VMs; this is not a dedicated CPU reservation.
Values.Hint: Processors for ContosoDC1. Minimum 2. CPU is shared across VMs; this is not a dedicated CPU reservation.

Values.Group: 2. Azure host VM - super-host for the domain controller, admin station and Azure Local nodes
Values.Label: DC RAM (GB, minimum 2)
Values.Description: Static RAM for ContosoDC1. Minimum 2 GB. Increase if the lab has spare memory.
Values.Hint: Static RAM for ContosoDC1. Minimum 2 GB. Increase if the lab has spare memory.

Values.Group: 2. Azure host VM - super-host for the domain controller, admin station and Azure Local nodes
Values.Label: Admin station vCPUs (minimum 2)
Values.Description: Processors for the planned admin station. Minimum 2. CPU is shared across VMs.
Values.Hint: Processors for the planned admin station. Minimum 2. CPU is shared across VMs.

Values.Group: 2. Azure host VM - super-host for the domain controller, admin station and Azure Local nodes
Values.Label: Admin station RAM (GB, minimum 4)
Values.Description: Static RAM for the planned admin station. Minimum 4 GB.
Values.Hint: Static RAM for the planned admin station. Minimum 4 GB.

Values.Group: 2. Azure host VM - super-host for the domain controller, admin station and Azure Local nodes
Values.Label: Number of Azure Local nodes (2-16)
Values.Description: How many Azure Local node VMs the lab plans for (2 to 16, default 2). The SuperHost RAM and vCPU budget counts each node's RAM and vCPUs this many times, so memory is planned before the SuperHost is built. Names after NodeName2 are suggested by continuing the numbering (for example AzL2101Node3), and the node IP range must hold one address per node. Host Console step 9 starts with this many nodes and can still change it.
Values.Hint: 2 to 16. Budgets node RAM/vCPU on the SuperHost; Host Console step 9 can still change it.

Values.Group: 2. Azure host VM - super-host for the domain controller, admin station and Azure Local nodes
Values.Label: Each Azure Local node vCPUs (min 12)
Values.Description: Processors assigned equally to each node. Minimum 12 per node. The plan budgets the Number of Azure Local nodes above (default 2); Host Console step 9 can change it (2-16) and checks the host for that many before creating VMs.
Values.Hint: Processors assigned equally to each node. Minimum 12 per node. The plan budgets the Number of Azure Local nodes above (default 2); Host Console step 9 can change it (2-16) and checks the host for that many before creating VMs.

Values.Group: 2. Azure host VM - super-host for the domain controller, admin station and Azure Local nodes
Values.Label: Each Azure Local node RAM (GB, min 36)
Values.Description: Static RAM assigned equally to each node. Minimum 36 GB each. The plan budgets this value once per node in the Number of Azure Local nodes above (default 2); Host Console step 9 can change it (2-16) and stops before creating VMs if the host RAM cannot hold that many.
Values.Hint: Static RAM assigned equally to each node. Minimum 36 GB each. The plan budgets this value once per node in the Number of Azure Local nodes above (default 2); Host Console step 9 can change it (2-16) and stops before creating VMs if the host RAM cannot hold that many.

Values.Group: 2. Azure host VM - super-host for the domain controller, admin station and Azure Local nodes
Values.Label: Azure CLI - create host VM
Values.Description: Creates the host VM in the resource group created above, using this plan's subscription, VM name and administrator account. Region is fixed to southcentralus and size/available vCPUs to the section 2 selections. Default request: Standard_D48als_v7 with 20 available vCPUs (48 maximum). Refresh Azure sizes is optional for the default; CPU-support metadata produces nonblocking warnings; quota and capacity are separate checks. DOUBLE-CLICK to copy into interactive PowerShell after az login --tenant <tenant ID>, or Azure Cloud Shell (PowerShell). Azure CLI prompts for the administrator password; it is not stored in the plan. Includes Windows Server 2025 Gen2, a 256 GB OS disk and a 1024 GB data disk on Premium SSD. No inbound RDP rule is created. Check regional SKU availability, subscription quota and nested-virtualization support before deploying. This creates only the VM and its supporting resources: it does not add the restricted RDP rule or nightly shutdown from script 00. Use this command OR script 00 to create the host, not both. For Custom (on-premises), this host creation command is not applicable and cannot be copied; skip script 00.
Values.Hint: Double-click to copy; apply your identifier first. Password is prompted. RDP remains closed until an approved restricted rule is added.
Values.UsedIn: Interactive PowerShell on your workstation or Azure Cloud Shell, after creating the host resource group; alternative to script 00 VM creation
Values.Command: az vm create --subscription "{{SubscriptionId}}" --resource-group "{{HostResourceGroup}}" --name "{{HostVMName}}" --location southcentralus --size "{{HostVMSize}}" --v-cpus-available {{HostAvailableVcpus}} --image MicrosoftWindowsServer:WindowsServer:2025-datacenter-g2:latest --security-type TrustedLaunch --enable-secure-boot true --enable-vtpm true --admin-username "{{HostAdminName}}" --os-disk-size-gb 256 --storage-sku os=Premium_LRS 0=Premium_LRS --data-disk-sizes-gb 1024 --data-disk-caching None --public-ip-sku Standard --nsg-rule NONE --output json

Values.Group: 2. Azure host VM - super-host for the domain controller, admin station and Azure Local nodes
Values.Label: Azure VM administrator account
Values.Description: The administrator account created on the Azure host VM when it's deployed (script 00). You use it to sign in to the host VM with Remote Desktop. Azure blocks common names such as 'admin', 'administrator', 'user', 'root' and 'test'.
Values.Hint: 1-20 letters, numbers, . _ or - ; can't end with a period; can't be a reserved name like admin, administrator, user, root, guest or test
Values.UsedIn: 00.Workstation-CreateHostVM.ps1, Remote Desktop to the host VM

Values.Group: 2. Azure host VM - super-host for the domain controller, admin station and Azure Local nodes
Values.Label: Azure VM administrator password
Values.Value: Not recorded - you choose it when prompted
Values.Description: REMINDER: script 00 asks for this password when it creates the Azure host VM, and you use it every time you connect with Remote Desktop. For security, the Lab Builder does NOT record it - keep it somewhere safe, like a password manager.
Values.Hint: 12-123 characters, with at least 3 of: an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a number and a special character
Values.UsedIn: 00.Workstation-CreateHostVM.ps1, Remote Desktop to the host VM

Values.Label: Isolated cluster network
Values.Description: The private network inside the host VM that every lab machine uses (behind NAT). It must NOT overlap the Azure virtual network the host VM sits on (for example 172.16.0.0/16), or any network connected to it. The scripts use /24.
Values.Hint: A /24 network written as a.b.c.0/24

Values.Label: Default gateway
Values.Description: The host VM's address on the InternalSwitchNAT switch. Every lab machine uses it as its default gateway to reach the internet through NAT. Usually the first address in the network.
Values.Hint: An IPv4 address, e.g. 192.168.44.51 - must be inside the lab network and not used by anything else

Values.Label: Domain controller IP (DNS server)
Values.Description: ContosoDC1's static address. It's also the DNS server for every node, so the nodes and the deployment wizard point at it.
Values.Hint: An IPv4 address, e.g. 192.168.44.51 - must be inside the lab network and not used by anything else

Values.Label: DHCP range - first IP
Values.Description: Optional DHCP scope on ContosoDC1 for extra lab VMs. Azure Local nodes use static IPs. Must not overlap the node IP range or the cluster resources range.
Values.Hint: An IPv4 address, e.g. 192.168.44.51 - must be inside the lab network and not used by anything else

Values.Label: DHCP range - last IP
Values.Description: End of the optional DHCP scope on ContosoDC1.
Values.Hint: An IPv4 address, e.g. 192.168.44.51 - must be inside the lab network and not used by anything else

Values.Label: Resource group (Arc registration + cluster)
Values.Description: The Azure resource group the nodes are registered into with Azure Arc, and where the Azure Local cluster, its Key Vault and storage account are created. Best practice: ONE resource group per cluster, paired with the cluster's OU and LCM account - it keeps each cluster's Arc machines, Key Vault and other resources together, lets you assign permissions and policy exemptions to just that cluster, and lets you remove a cluster cleanly. The deployment roles (Key Vault, Storage, Arc onboarding) must be assigned on THIS resource group. Keep it separate from the host VM's resource group.
Values.Hint: 1-90 letters, numbers, . _ - ( )  and it can't end with a period
Values.UsedIn: 14.Node-ArcRegister.ps1, 13.Workstation-AzurePrereqs.ps1, 15.Workstation-PolicyReview.ps1, deployment wizard, Azure-Prep.ps1 (Lab Builder Azure buttons)

Values.Label: Region
Values.Description: The Azure region the nodes register in and the cluster is deployed to. It must be a region that supports Azure Local, and the Arc registration and the deployment must use the same one. Written in lowercase with no spaces - the region's 'name', not its display name (southcentralus, not South Central US). Also used for the host VM.
Values.Hint: Lowercase letters and numbers only, no spaces (e.g. eastus, southcentralus, westeurope)

Values.Label: Azure Local cluster name
Values.Description: The name of the Azure Local instance (the cluster). It's also created as a computer object (cluster name object) in Active Directory, in the cluster's OU, so it follows Windows computer name rules: 15 characters or less.
Values.Hint: 1-15 letters, numbers or hyphens, starting with a letter or number

Values.Label: Azure Local image release
Values.Description: Which Azure Local release image (ISO) the host downloads and installs the nodes from, as YYMM: 2608 = August 2026. The host downloads https://aka.ms/hcireleaseimage/<release> to C:\ISO\AzureLocal-<release>.iso; an ISO already in C:\ISO for the same release is used as is. Choose it before Prepare data disk (01) and Create node VMs (10). To move an existing lab to a newer version without a different ISO, set Target solution version below instead.
Values.Hint: Pick 2601 to 2611 from the list (YYMM). 2611 may not be published yet - if its download fails, use Open page / the Azure portal, or choose 2610.

Values.Label: Target solution version (optional)
Values.Description: OPTIONAL. The Azure Local solution version the nodes are brought to when they register with Azure Arc (script 14), so you can plan to roll forward to a newer release without downloading a different ISO. Format Major.YYMM.Build.Revision: in 12.2610.1004.50, 12 is the major line (OS 26100 / 24H2), 2610 is the October 2026 release train, 1004 is the build family and 50 is the revision. Other published examples: 12.2604.1003.1006 and 12.2602.1002.501. For a newer release, copy the full version from the Microsoft Learn page Azure Local release information - do not guess the build or revision. Leave it blank to pick from a list on each node when script 14 runs. The Node Console box Target version (next Arc run) overrides it on one node.
Values.Hint: Blank (pick on the node), or four numbers like 12.2610.1004.50 (Major.YYMM.Build.Revision)

Values.Label: Azure CLI - create cluster resource group
Values.Description: One line that creates the Azure Local CLUSTER resource group - one per cluster. The nodes register into it with Azure Arc, and the cluster, Key vault, witness storage account and custom location are created in it. Built from the values in groups 1 and 4, so it updates as you change them. DOUBLE-CLICK to copy. Then assign the deployment roles on it (button '2. Assign roles on RG'). Safe to run again.
Values.Hint: Double-click to copy
Values.UsedIn: Your workstation or Azure Cloud Shell, before script 13

Values.Label: Azure CLI - assign deployment roles on the cluster resource group
Values.Command: $u = az ad signed-in-user show --query id -o tsv; foreach ($r in 'Key Vault Data Access Administrator','Key Vault Secrets Officer','Key Vault Contributor','Storage Account Contributor','Azure Connected Machine Onboarding','Azure Connected Machine Resource Administrator') { az role assignment create --assignee-object-id $u --assignee-principal-type User --role $r --scope /subscriptions/{{SubscriptionId}}/resourceGroups/{{ClusterResourceGroup}} -o none; "$r - assigned" }
Values.Description: One line that assigns the 6 Azure Local deployment roles to YOU (the signed-in account) on the CLUSTER resource group ONLY: Key Vault Data Access Administrator, Key Vault Secrets Officer, Key Vault Contributor, Storage Account Contributor, Azure Connected Machine Onboarding and Azure Connected Machine Resource Administrator. Owner or Contributor alone is NOT enough - without the Key Vault roles the wizard shows 'Insufficient permissions at resource group level'. Subscription-level roles (Azure Stack HCI Administrator, Reader) are NOT included - use button '2. Assign roles on RG' or the Azure prep commands file for those. DOUBLE-CLICK to copy, then paste into PowerShell after 'az login --tenant <tenant ID>' and 'az account set --subscription <subscription ID>'. You need Owner or User Access Administrator. Safe to run again. Sign out of the portal and back in afterwards.
Values.Hint: Double-click to copy. Run in PowerShell (it uses a PowerShell loop), after az login.
Values.UsedIn: Your workstation or Azure Cloud Shell (PowerShell), after the cluster resource group exists

Values.Label: Azure prep commands - resource groups, roles, policy review
Values.Description: Creates AzurePrep-Commands.txt in the rollout folder, filled in with your values, and opens it. It walks through, step by step: 1. sign in and select the subscription, 2. create BOTH resource groups (host VM and cluster), 3. register the resource providers, 4. assign the deployment roles on the cluster resource group and the subscription, 5. a reminder - with a quick command - to REVIEW AZURE POLICY before registering the nodes. Paste one step at a time into PowerShell or Azure Cloud Shell. 'Roll out scripts' creates the same file.
Values.Hint: Double-click to create and open the file. Needs Owner or User Access Administrator for the role steps.
Values.UsedIn: Your workstation or Azure Cloud Shell, before script 00

Values.Label: Domain NetBIOS name
Values.Description: The short (NetBIOS) name of the lab domain, used for sign-ins like CONTOSOLAB\Administrator. 07dc.DC-CreateForest.ps1 creates the domain with this name and the domain name in section 7 (Management - Domain). Usually the first part of the domain name in capitals. Choose it before 07dc runs - it cannot be changed afterwards.
Values.Hint: 1-15 letters, numbers or hyphens, with at least one letter, e.g. CONTOSOLAB

Values.Label: OU path for this cluster
Values.Description: The Active Directory OU that holds this cluster's node computer objects, cluster name object and LCM account. Best practice: ONE OU per cluster. Written as a distinguished name - read it right to left: DC=local,DC=contosolab is the domain, OU=LABcluster2101 is the OU.
Values.Hint: Starts with OU=, ends with the domain (DC=...), and can't contain & " ' < >

Values.Label: LCM deployment account
Values.Description: The Active Directory account the deployment (and later updates and node repairs) uses. Best practice: ONE LCM account per cluster, paired with the cluster's OU. Enter the username only - no domain prefix.
Values.Hint: 1-20 letters, numbers, - or _ ; can't start with a number or '-'; can't be 'admin'; must differ from the local admin account

Values.Label: LCM account password
Values.Value: Not recorded - you choose it when prompted
Values.Description: REMINDER: the LCM deployment account needs a password. You set it when 09dc.DC-PrepareADForAzureLocal.ps1 asks, and you type it again in the Azure portal deployment wizard. For security, the Lab Builder does NOT record it - keep it somewhere safe, like a password manager.
Values.Hint: 14+ characters with an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a number and a special character

Values.Label: 1. Administrator account (built-in)
Values.Description: The built-in Administrator account exists on every node by default. You use it for the FIRST sign-in after installing the Azure Local OS, when Windows asks you to set its password. 11.Host-PrepareNodes.ps1 also signs in with it (PowerShell Direct) to rename the NICs and copy files. Its name can't be changed here.
Values.Hint: Built-in - exists on every node by default
Values.UsedIn: First sign-in after the OS install, 11.Host-PrepareNodes.ps1

Values.Label: Administrator password
Values.Value: Not recorded - you choose it when prompted
Values.Description: REMINDER: you set the built-in Administrator password at the first sign-in after installing the OS. Use the SAME password on every node - 11.Host-PrepareNodes.ps1 asks for it once and uses it for all nodes. For security, the Lab Builder does NOT record it.
Values.Hint: 14+ characters with an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a number and a special character; same on every node
Values.UsedIn: First sign-in after the OS install, 11.Host-PrepareNodes.ps1

Values.Label: 2. Second local admin account (recommended)
Values.Description: An OPTIONAL second local administrator account, created on every node by 12.Node-Configure.ps1 with the same password on each node. Recommended for the cluster deployment: enter it in the Azure portal deployment wizard as the local administrator, instead of the built-in Administrator. It must not have the same name as the built-in Administrator or the LCM account.
Values.Hint: 1-20 letters, numbers, . _ or - ; not 'Administrator'; different from the LCM account

Values.Label: Second local admin password
Values.Description: The password for the second local admin account (Loc2admin), the SAME on every node. If you enter it here, 'Roll out scripts' injects it into 12.Node-Configure.ps1, so each node is configured without typing it. Leave it EMPTY to have 12.Node-Configure.ps1 ask for it on each node instead. You also enter it in the Azure portal deployment wizard as the local administrator password. 'Export for sharing' empties this value.
Values.Hint: 14+ characters with an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a number and a special character; no single quote ('). Saved in plain text.

Values.Label: Node 1 name
Values.Description: The Hyper-V VM name and the Windows computer name of the first Azure Local node. It becomes the Azure Arc machine name in the cluster resource group. 15 characters or less.
Values.Hint: 1-15 letters, numbers or hyphens, starting with a letter or number

Values.Label: Node 2 name
Values.Description: The Hyper-V VM name and the Windows computer name of the second Azure Local node. Must be different from node 1.
Values.Hint: 1-15 letters, numbers or hyphens, starting with a letter or number; different from node 1
An IPv4 address, e.g. 192.168.44.51 - must be inside the lab network and not used by anything else
Values.Label: Node IP range - first IP
Values.Description: Node IP range: the static management IPs for the Azure Local nodes, set on each node's 1-MGMTCOMP1 adapter. Node 1 gets the first address, node 2 the next, and so on (.51, .52, .53...). 192.168.44.51 - .59 leaves room for up to 9 nodes. Must not overlap the cluster resources range or the DHCP range.
Values.UsedIn: 11.Host-PrepareNodes.ps1 (fills in 12.Node-Configure.ps1 for each node), deployment wizard

Values.Hint: An IPv4 address, e.g. 192.168.44.51 - must be inside the lab network and not used by anything else
Values.Label: Node IP range - last IP
Values.Description: End of the node IP range. It needs one address per planned node (Number of Azure Local nodes in section 2, default 2, up to 16) and per node chosen in Host Console step 9; Apply node names refuses more nodes than the range holds.

Values.Label: Cluster resources range - first IP
Values.Description: Cluster resources range: the infrastructure IP range Azure Local uses for cluster resources (cluster IP, Arc resource bridge and other services). Entered in the deployment wizard. It needs at least 6 consecutive free addresses that no node, the DC or DHCP uses. 192.168.44.61 - .69 gives 9.
Values.Hint: An IPv4 address, e.g. 192.168.44.51 - must be inside the lab network and not used by anything else

Values.Label: Cluster resources range - last IP
Values.Description: End of the cluster resources range. 192.168.44.61 to .69 is 9 addresses (the minimum is 6).
Values.Hint: An IPv4 address, e.g. 192.168.44.51 - must be inside the lab network and not used by anything else

Values.Label: Basics - Key vault name
Values.Description: Basics tab. The deployment creates a NEW Key vault in the cluster resource group to store the deployment secrets. The name must be unique across ALL of Azure, so add something unique for each lab or student. Your account needs the Key Vault roles on the resource group (script 13). (The wizard also asks for values tracked above: subscription, resource group, region, cluster name, OU, LCM account, local admin, gateway, DNS and the cluster resources IP range.)
Values.Hint: 3-24 letters, numbers or hyphens; starts with a letter; can't end with a hyphen; unique across Azure

Values.Label: Networking - Storage connectivity
Values.Description: Networking tab. How the nodes' storage NICs connect. In this lab they connect through the StorageSwitch (a Hyper-V private switch), so choose 'Network switch for storage'. 'No switch for storage' (switchless) is for nodes cabled directly to each other.
Values.Pattern: ^(Network switch for storage|No switch for storage)$
Values.Hint: Network switch for storage  or  No switch for storage

Values.Label: Networking - Traffic grouping
Values.Description: Networking tab. How traffic types are grouped into network intents. This lab uses 2 intents: management + compute together on 1-MGMTCOMP1/2, and storage on its own on 3-STORAGE1/2.
Values.Hint: The wizard option matching your NIC layout

Values.Label: Networking - Management + compute adapters
Values.Description: Networking tab. The adapters for the management + compute intent. The names match Hyper-V because 11.Host-PrepareNodes.ps1 renamed the NICs inside each node.
Values.Hint: Adapter names as shown inside the nodes

Values.Label: Networking - Storage adapters
Values.Description: Networking tab. The adapters for the storage intent, connected to the StorageSwitch.
Values.Hint: Adapter names as shown inside the nodes

Values.Label: Networking - Storage VLAN 1
Values.Description: Networking tab. VLAN ID for the first storage network. 711 is the wizard's default. The node NICs are set to trunk VLANs 0-1000 (script 10), so any ID in that range works.
Values.Hint: 1-1000 (the node NICs trunk VLANs 0-1000)

Values.Label: Networking - Storage VLAN 2
Values.Description: Networking tab. VLAN ID for the second storage network. 712 is the wizard's default. Must be different from storage VLAN 1.
Values.Hint: 1-1000; different from storage VLAN 1

Values.Label: Networking - RDMA (customize network settings)
Values.Description: Networking tab -> Customize network settings. The nodes' NICs are virtual and have no RDMA, so set RDMA (Network Direct) to Disabled for both intents in this nested lab. Physical servers with RDMA NICs leave it on.
Values.Hint: Disabled for this nested lab

Values.Label: Networking - IP allocation
Values.Description: Networking tab. Manual = you type the cluster resources IP range, subnet mask, gateway and DNS server (all tracked in '3. Lab network'). There's no DHCP for the cluster in this lab.
Values.Hint: Manual for this lab

Values.Label: Networking - Subnet mask
Values.Description: Networking tab. The subnet mask of the lab network - 255.255.255.0 for a /24 network like 192.168.44.0/24.
Values.Hint: 255.255.255.0 for a /24 network

Values.Label: Management - Custom location name
Values.Description: Management tab. The custom location is the Azure resource you'll pick later when creating VMs and other workloads on this cluster. Created in the cluster resource group.
Values.Hint: 1-63 letters, numbers, . or -

Values.Label: Management - Cloud witness storage account
Values.Description: Management tab. A 2-node cluster needs a witness to decide which node keeps running if they lose contact. The deployment creates an Azure storage account as a cloud witness. The name must be unique across ALL of Azure, so add something unique for each lab or student.
Values.Hint: 3-24 LOWERCASE letters and numbers only; unique across Azure

Values.Label: Management - Domain
Values.Description: Management tab. The Active Directory domain the nodes join. 07dc.DC-CreateForest.ps1 creates it, and the other lab scripts use it. Choose it before 07dc runs - the OU path in section 5 must end with this domain.
Values.Hint: A domain name with at least one dot, e.g. contosolab.local

Values.Label: Security - Security settings
Values.Description: Security tab. Recommended applies Microsoft's security baseline (BitLocker, WDAC, drift control and more). Customized lets you turn individual settings off - use it if a setting fails in the nested lab.
Values.Hint: Recommended security settings  or  Customized security settings

Values.Label: Advanced - Volumes
Values.Value: Create workload volumes and required infrastructure volumes
Values.Description: Advanced tab. The recommended option creates the infrastructure volume plus a workload volume per node, ready for VMs. The other option creates only the infrastructure volume.
Values.Example: Create workload volumes and required infrastructure volumes
Values.Hint: The wizard option to use

Values.Label: Admin station name
Values.Description: The admin station's name - used for BOTH the VM name in Hyper-V Manager and its Windows computer name, like ContosoDC1 for the domain controller. The admin station is a management server inside the lab, joined to the domain, where you run Failover Cluster Manager, Hyper-V Manager and the AD and DNS tools against the cluster - the way you'd manage a real Azure Local cluster, rather than signing in to the nodes. 15 characters or less.
Values.Hint: 1-15 letters, numbers or hyphens, starting with a letter or number

Values.Label: Admin station IP
Values.Description: The admin station's static IP on the lab network. It uses the domain controller for DNS.
Values.Hint: An IPv4 address, e.g. 192.168.44.51 - must be inside the lab network and not used by anything else
